title: Practise Now 8(2)
summary: Prove the right angle with the Converse, then use it to find TX.
alt: Practise Now 8(2): XYZ is a plot of land such that XY = 45 m, YZ = 24 m and XZ = 51 m. (i) Show that ∠XYZ = 90°. (ii) A tree T is located on ZY such that ZT = 14 m. Find TX, the distance of the tree from X.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: **XYZ** is a plot of land with **XY = 45 m**, **YZ = 24 m** and **XZ = 51 m**. (i) Show that **∠XYZ = 90°**. (ii) A tree **T** lies on **ZY** such that **ZT = 14 m**. Find **TX**.

steps.title: Find the longest side
steps.narration: The **longest side** is **XZ = 51 m**. If ΔXYZ is right-angled, XZ must be the **hypotenuse** — the side opposite the right angle.

steps.title: Square and add the other two sides
steps.narration: Square **XY** and **YZ**, then add them.\[\begin{aligned}XY^2 + YZ^2 &= 45^2 + 24^2 \\ &= 2025 + 576 = 2601\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Compare and conclude
steps.narration: Since **XZ^2 = XY^2 + YZ^2** (2601 = 2601), by the **Converse of Pythagoras' Theorem**, ΔXYZ **is** a right-angled triangle, where **∠Y = 90°**.

steps.title: (ii) Find TY
steps.narration: **T** lies on **ZY** with **ZT = 14 m**, so **TY** is what is left of **ZY**.\[\begin{aligned}TY &= ZY - ZT \\ &= 24 - 14 = 10\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔXYT, **∠Y = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **TX**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. (∠XYT is the same right angle as ∠XYZ, since T lies on ZY.) **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TX^2} &= \role{legA}{XY^2} + \role{legB}{TY^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and add
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and add.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TX^2} &= \role{legA}{XY^2} + \role{legB}{TY^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{45^2} + \role{legB}{10^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{2025} + \role{legB}{100} \\ &= \role{hyp}{2125}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 2125 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TX^2} &= \role{legA}{XY^2} + \role{legB}{TY^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{45^2} + \role{legB}{10^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{2025} + \role{legB}{100} \\ &= \role{hyp}{2125} \\ \role{hyp}{TX} &= \sqrt{2125} = \role{ans}{46.1\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Check TY
challenges.prompt: ZY = 24 m and ZT = 14 m. Find TY.

takeaways: Find the **longest side** first — if the triangle is right-angled, that side must be the hypotenuse.
Test it: does the longest side's **square** equal the **sum of the squares** of the other two sides?
If the squares match, the triangle **is** right-angled (opposite the longest side); if not, it isn't.
Once the right angle is confirmed, Pythagoras' theorem works in **any** right-angled triangle built from it.

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always find the **longest side** first — only that side could possibly be the hypotenuse.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
